# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to relay the manual to Deaf, who can then identify the specified wire colours and key markings and tell Blind the exact sequence. I’ll use distinct gestures as operation markers, with repeated thumbs-up gestures encoding the key numbers and distinct tokens for purple and red.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🫰", "👆", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "🤏", "🤜", "👆", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use gestures to tell Deaf: report DISPLAY, LIGHT, STRIP, KEYPAD, and WIRES in that order, then relay the manual's required operation. Code: 👍 means press, 🤏 means cut; use ☝ for position 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, and 🖖 for 4. Have Deaf speak the visual facts to me on the next turn.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb readings: display 9; light green; painted strip red blue green. Keypad buttons: 1=1, 2=4, 3=7, 4=2; requires 2 digits; currently entered nothing. Wires: 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Please use the manual to determine the exact action and tell Blind.

The required sequence is cut the purple wire (wire 6), press keypad position 3 (the key marked 7), cut the red wire (wire 4), then press keypad position 2 (the key marked 4). I’ll encode wire numbers by repeating the position-1 symbol, and keypad positions with the agreed symbols.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍", "🤟", "🤏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send me the manual's exact operation now: press slot 1-4 or cut wire position 1-6. Include all needed interpretation of the visual details.
Deaf says to Mute: Updated readings: display 6 and light red. Strip remains red blue green; keypad remains buttons 1=1, 2=4, 3=7, 4=2, requires 2 digits, entered nothing; wires remain 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Please read the manual and speak the exact safe action to Blind.

The safe sequence is: cut wire 6 (purple), press keypad slot 3 (the key marked 7), cut wire 4 (red), then press keypad slot 2 (the key marked 4). I cannot speak to Blind directly, so I will send Deaf the established gesture encoding for Deaf to relay aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍", "🤟", "🤏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the exact safe action from the manual. Please state press slot number or cut wire position, using the current display 6 and red light.
Deaf says to Mute: Current readings: display 0; light green. Strip red blue green. Keypad 1=1, 2=4, 3=7, 4=2; two digits; entered nothing. Wires 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Please send the manual's exact action using the code I am showing: count ☝ gestures for each digit, 👍 between digits, 🤟 means enter keypad code, ✌ means cut wire, 👌 means turn or press a control. Use 🤏 to start each instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤏 ☝ 👍 🤟]

The current display and light do not alter the manual’s fixed sequence. I will encode the four exact instructions: cut wire 6, press keypad slot 3, cut wire 4, press keypad slot 2. Each instruction begins with 🤏; ✌ marks a cut, 👌 a press, and the number of ☝ gestures gives the position.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "👌", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please give the final safe action from the manual for current display 0 and green light. Reply literally as either PRESS slot 1, PRESS slot 2, PRESS slot 3, PRESS slot 4, or CUT wire position 1 through 6. Do not use gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: I decoded your gestures as cut wire 6, operate control 3, cut wire 4, operate control 2. Please speak to Blind and clarify whether each operate instruction means press a keypad button or turn another control, and give the exact safe order.

The manual requires cutting wire 6, pressing keypad slot 3 (the key marked 7), cutting wire 4, then pressing keypad slot 2 (the key marked 4). The “operate” steps are keypad presses, not turning another control. I’ll send Deaf the established press/cut code so Deaf can state this aloud to Blind.

```text

```

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Clarify the two operations in the sequence: after cutting wire 6, is control 3 pressed or another action? After cutting wire 4, is control 2 pressed or another action? State the exact four literal calls in order.
Deaf says to Mute: Your latest gestures decode under our code as 73 and 63, but they contain no action symbol and no enter marker. Please speak to Blind with the exact required operation, and use the agreed symbols only for a clear instruction.

The exact actions are: cut wire 6; press keypad slot 3; cut wire 4; press keypad slot 2. I’ll distinguish keypad presses with 👌 and the keypad-code marker 🤟, while using ✌ for cuts and counting wire or slot positions with ☝.

```text

```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not use gestures or numeric shorthand. State the exact safe action sequence in words for the current readings: display 2, blue light, strip red-blue-green, keypad labels 1=1, 2=4, 3=7, 4=2, and wires 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Clarify whether operate control means press a keypad slot, and include any required two-digit entry and enter action.

I cannot speak to Blind directly. The manual gives four actions only: cut wire 6, press keypad slot 3 (label 7), cut wire 4, then press keypad slot 2 (label 4). No separate enter action is stated; the two keypad presses are the required two-digit entry. I’ll send Deaf an unambiguous action-coded message so Deaf can say those words aloud.
